cards.text: Mary and Joseph's baby Boy is eight days old, so it's time for His circumcision. It's also time for His name: Jesus. Now, friend, most parents argue over baby names for MONTHS.

cards.question: Mary and Joseph came up with the name Jesus on their own.

cards.text: Then the time of purification under the Law of Moses is complete. So His parents pack up the baby and hit the road to present Him to the Lord.

cards.question: Mary and Joseph bring baby Jesus to ___ to present Him to the Lord.

cards.text: Why the trip? The Law of the Lord has something to say about a family's very first baby boy.

cards.question: The Law of the Lord says every ___ male shall be consecrated to the Lord.
The Law of the Lord also specifies a sacrifice for this visit. What is it?

answers.text: A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons
A young bull or two spotless goats
A year-old lamb or a young ram

cards.text: Now meet Simeon, a man in Jerusalem. He's righteous, he's devout, the Holy Spirit is upon him, and he's waiting for the consolation of Israel. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to open it, so believe me, I RESPECT a man who waits.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit has revealed something to Simeon about his waiting. What is it?

answers.text: He won't see death before seeing the Lord's Christ
He'll serve as high priest before he dies
He'll see the temple rebuilt in his lifetime

cards.text: Now watch the timing on this, baker. Mary and Joseph carry baby Jesus into the temple courts to do what the Law requires, and Simeon is right there.

cards.question: Simeon ends up in the temple courts that day just by chance.

cards.text: Simeon takes the baby in his arms and blesses God. Me? Somebody hands me a baby and all I've got is a mustache, so I'm holding that child like a HOT cookie tray, sweating the whole time.

cards.question: Simeon tells God He can now dismiss His servant in peace. Why can Simeon say that?

answers.text: His eyes have seen God's salvation
His years of temple work are done
His family is finally safe at home

cards.question: Simeon says God prepared this salvation in the sight of all people. It's a light for revelation to the ___ and glory to God's people Israel.

cards.text: Mary and Joseph are amazed at what's been said about their Child. Can you blame them? Last time somebody picked ME up, I ended up in the back of a junk drawer.
Then Simeon blesses them and turns to Mary. He's got more to say about this Child, and not all of it is easy to hear.

cards.question: Simeon tells Mary what her Child is appointed to cause in Israel. What is it?

answers.text: The rise and fall of many
A new king for every tribe

cards.question: Simeon tells Mary that everyone in Israel will speak well of her Child.

cards.text: Through this Child, Simeon says, the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed. Then he has a word for Mary herself.

cards.question: Simeon tells Mary that a ___ will pierce her soul as well.

cards.text: Now meet Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She's well along in years, and she had been married for seven years.

cards.question: After those seven years of marriage, Anna was a widow to the age of ___.
Anna the prophetess is in the temple the day Jesus is brought in. Where does she spend her days?

answers.text: She travels from town to town
She stays at home in Asher

cards.text: Anna worships night and day, fasting and praying. Night AND day, friend, and I can't stay awake through a twelve-minute oven timer.
Then Anna comes forward at that very moment. Talk about TIMING.

cards.question: When Anna comes forward to the Child, what does she do first?

answers.text: She asks Simeon for a blessing
She brings a gift for the Child

cards.question: Anna speaks about the Child to all who were waiting for the ___ of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Mary and Joseph do everything the Law of the Lord requires. Then it's time to head home.

cards.question: Their business at the temple is done. Where do Mary and Joseph take Jesus home to?

cards.text: And the Child grows and becomes strong. Same baby Simeon held in his arms, baker, growing up right before our eyes.

cards.question: As Jesus grows, He is filled with wisdom, and the grace of God is upon Him.

findings.problem: The joke 'most parents argue over baby names for MONTHS' is a joke built on parents, which the audience rule lists as off-limits.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: 'a family's very first baby boy' gives away 'firstborn', the answer to the fill in the blank on card 6.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question asks what sacrifice the Law of the Lord specifies for this visit. The wrong answer 'A year-old lamb or a young ram' is partly what the Law specifies for purification (Lev 12:6, a year-old lamb), so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'to do what the Law requires' renames what Luke 2:27 calls 'what was customary under the Law'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences ('…blesses God.' / 'Me?' / 'Somebody hands me…'). It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 2:29-30, but the right answer ('His eyes have seen God's salvation') comes only from Luke 2:30.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action. Mary and Joseph are amazed at what's been said about their Child, but the comparison is about being picked up and ending up in a junk drawer. 'Can you blame them?' doesn't follow, and the line also loosely ties being picked up (as Simeon picked up Jesus) to being thrown away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'not all of it is easy to hear' rules out the all-positive wrong answers on card 3 ('Peace in every town', 'A new king for every tribe') and points to False on card 4.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the exact word of Simeon's line (sword, thorn or arrow). Each one could pierce, so nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'When Anna comes forward to the Child' adds who she comes forward to. Luke 2:38 says only 'Coming forward at that moment.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
